clue.text: They're very hard for suckers to enjoy!

definitions.text: They're very hard for suckers to enjoy!

parts.words: They're very hard for suckers to enjoy!
parts.note: the 'suckers' sound like dupes, but they are simply people sucking confectionery

explanation.surface: A warning that some things are too tough for gullible people to like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suckers' wants to mean fools; here it means people who suck their sweets slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard confectionery made from boiled sugar is meant to be sucked, not chewed.

clue.text: Showers under Beachy Head, showing imagination

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece written under another comes after it, so the showers follow the head
the head of a word is its first letter, here the start of Beachy

parts.note: showers of water from the sky are rain

explanation.surface: Rain falling below the white cliffs of Beachy Head on the south coast of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Beachy Head is a chalk headland in Sussex, which makes 'Head' read as part of a place name; it picks the B of Beachy.
explanation.definitionFit: Brain is used for mental power and inventiveness, as in 'use your brain'.

clue.text: Nice tax form — but inaccurate!

indicators.note: to form something is to shape it, so the letters of the two words are moulded into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that a nicely filled tax return is wrong all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' looks like a tax form; it is the anagram signal on NICE and TAX.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean not exact or correct; synonyms.

clue.text: Turned up to cold dish without steak

indicators.note: an old sense of without is outside, so the dish goes round the other letters

parts.note: an entree is a dish served as a main or intermediate course
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: in a down clue turning a word up reads it from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a steak and asks for a cold dish instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, an old sense, so the dish wraps round the cold letter and the turned word; 'Turned up' reverses 'to' only.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrecote is a cut of beef from between the ribs; an example of steak.

clue.text: See 1
It was designed for the middle of a ship

indicators.note: something designed has been planned and laid out, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A remark about a feature built into the centre of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' looks like part of the ship talk; it rearranges IT WAS.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing ship the waist is the part of the deck between forecastle and quarterdeck.

clue.text: Way rope is mounted round number of ships abroad

indicators.note: the reversed way and rope go round, enclosing the number
in a down clue something mounted climbs upward, so the words before it are read from the bottom

parts.note: ST, street, is a way or road
X is the Roman numeral ten, a number

explanation.surface: Rigging talk about rope rising around a fleet of ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ships' looks like a noun, the fleet, but is the verb of the definition; 'is mounted' reverses STROPE to EPORTS, which 'round' wraps about X.
explanation.definitionFit: To export is to send goods overseas, which is shipping them abroad.

clue.text: Sent our bananas to us, requiring much effort

indicators.note: added to means the next word is attached after the anagram
going bananas is going crazy, so the letters of the words before it go wild

explanation.surface: Shipping a cargo of bananas to us was hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the cargo but is the anagram signal: SENT OUR becomes STRENUO, and US is added on.
explanation.definitionFit: Strenuous work is arduous, taking great exertion; synonym.

clue.text: Joke a month about royalty

indicators.note: the month goes about the joke, holding it inside

parts.note: May is a month of the year
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A jest made for a month about the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty is royal power and the title of a sovereign, standing for royalty.

clue.text: To amuse himself drunk prods it

indicators.note: someone drunk is all over the place, so the letters of the fodder are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunk poking things for his own entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like a description of the man; it is the anagram signal on PRODS IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To disport oneself is to frolic or divert oneself; synonym for entertaining oneself.

clue.text: So presses dresses to take back?

indicators.note: to dress is to arrange or set in order, as troops are dressed, so the letters are realigned

explanation.surface: Laundry: pressing dresses so as to take them back to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dresses' looks like clothing but is a verb here, the anagram signal on SO PRESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To repossess is to reclaim goods for non-payment, taking them back.

clue.text: Fight to get band to show evidence of contract?

parts.note: an engagement is a battle or fight between forces
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A fight, then a band appears, as proof of an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' is the marriage contract, and the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring worn after agreeing to marry is a sign of that promised union.

clue.text: See 11
Saying low races are to be housed

indicators.note: the races are housed inside the low noise, held within it

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Lowly races are to be given housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the cow's noise, not humble; TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle races.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto is a short maxim or saying adopted as a rule.

clue.text: Being into marriage it's right to look up "dominatrix"

indicators.note: the pieces are inside the marriage word, so they are being put into it

parts.note: a match is a marriage

indicators.note: in a down clue a word looking up is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance, as in an air of calm

explanation.surface: A married person relishes looking at a dominatrix.
explanation.walkthrough: AIR reversed by 'up' gives RIA; with R added it makes RIAR, which goes into MATCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dominant women; a matriarch rules a family as the female head.

clue.text: Neglect to ring church

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
a mission is a church or chapel set up by missionaries

explanation.surface: Failing to telephone the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like phoning; it is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglect, a failure to do something, is an omission; synonym.

clue.text: One warlike pit leader admitted "it's fair"

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the pit's first letter is let in to the warlike word

parts.note: martial means warlike

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here the start of pit

explanation.surface: A belligerent mine boss conceded that it was fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pit leader' sounds like a colliery boss; it is just P, admitted into MARTIAL after its M.
explanation.definitionFit: Impartial means unbiased, treating all sides equally; synonym of fair.

clue.text: Gummed labels showing the Queen in Staffs

indicators.note: the Queen goes in the staffs, inside them

parts.note: staffs are sticks
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Stamps bearing the Queen in Staffordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staffs' looks like the abbreviation of Staffordshire, an English county; here it is staves, STICKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stickers are adhesive labels; synonym.

clue.text: Stiff accountant died before Vera moved

indicators.note: the accountant and died come before the rest in the answer

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

indicators.note: the letters of the name are moved about

explanation.surface: A stiff accountant died before Vera moved house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' looks like a description of the accountant but is the definition; 'moved' makes AVER from VERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff is slang for a corpse, a dead body.

clue.text: Performs cup final songs

indicators.note: the final of a word is its last letter, here the end of cup

parts.note: lays are songs or ballads

explanation.surface: A band plays songs at the cup final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cup final' looks like a football match; it gives just P.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform music or drama is to play it.

clue.text: Gas bombs etc I found in North America

parts.note: ammo, ammunition, covers bombs and the like

indicators.note: I is found inside the abbreviation for the continent

explanation.surface: Bombs and the gas I discovered in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonia is a pungent gas of nitrogen and hydrogen; an example of a gas.

clue.text: Minds unwritten improvisation when this is played?

indicators.note: improvising makes something up freely, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Improvised music played without a written score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwritten improvisation' looks like music played by ear; 'improvisation' is the anagram signal on MINDS UNWRITTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A flute or trumpet, sounded by breath, is a thing that is played.

clue.text: See 20
Out of place at home being topless, wept

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone who wept, feeling out of place at home without a top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' cuts the W from WEPT, leaving EPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means unsuitable or inappropriate, out of place.

clue.text: One tends to manage to return empty syringe

indicators.note: returning sends the word back on itself, read backwards

parts.note: to run is to manage

indicators.note: an emptied word loses its inside, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A medic managing to bring back an empty syringe.
explanation.walkthrough: RUN reversed gives NUR; the first and last letters of syringe give SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after the sick; 'tends' is the verb of caring.

clue.text: Private showing of piano music and sketches

parts.note: P is the musical notation for piano, quietly
a review in the old spelling of revue is a show of songs and sketches

explanation.surface: A private performance of piano music and sketches.
explanation.walkthrough: A revue is a variety show; it was spelt 'review' in English before the French spelling took over.
explanation.definitionFit: A preview is a showing of a film or show before public release.

clue.text: Trespassers will be shot on board!

annotationWithheld.why: Trespassers will be shot on board! - the parse puts INNER (a shot hitting the target board) inside SS, but 'on board' would be both the container signal and the only source of SS, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Trespassers will be shot on board!

clue.text: Difficult to satisfy, the pals adore going out

indicators.note: going out on the town, the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Friends who love going out are hard to please.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' looks like nightlife; it is the anagram signal on THE PALS ADORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fussy and demanding is not easily satisfied.

clue.text: See 25
